A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an algorithm that combines multiple sequence alignments with network topology to cluster sequences into groups of related sequences.
we present a new approach to sequence clustering that combines network topology, sequence alignment and sequence conservation.

we have developed a method that clusters high-quality sequence alignments based on their network topology and multiple sequence alignment (MSA) likelihood, and we have applied the method to a set of alignments of the 20 human protein kinase (PK) domains in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) and the 20 PKs in the Human Protein Atlas (HPA).
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not necessary to use a complex model to get a good estimate for the number of clusters, and that a simple method can be used to obtain a reliable estimate of the cluster sizes.
it is possible to cluster sequences in a meaningful way by combining network topology and multiple sequence alignment likelihood.
the use of multiple alignment likelihoods can be used to improve the accuracy of sequence clustering.
